collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: The children ask an elder to defend an old coconut-husking title nobody remembers: defend the title, or retire undefeated.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has always said that, long ago, (subject.he/she) was the undefeated coconut-husking champion of the whole village: faster than anyone, three years running. Nobody alive remembers that contest. Nobody remembers it not happening, either. Today the children have organized a husking contest, and have asked the champion to defend (subject.his/her) title.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) rolls up (subject.his/her) sleeves. (subject.He/she) is genuinely, surprisingly fast, though not the fastest: (teen), a teenager, wins by a whisker. (subject) shakes the winner's hand and announces the end of a great era. The children are thrilled to have been there for it. Whether the great era ever happened doesn't seem to matter to anybody.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "A champion," says (subject), "knows when to retire." (subject.He/she) agrees to judge instead, and does so with enormous seriousness, giving every child expert advice. The champion's record remains unbeaten forever, mostly because nobody can check it.
